newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* From September through March, U.S. consumer spending grew at an annual rate of 4.9 percent, the biggest six-month rise this decade.
* U.S. Treasury prices rose as economic reports indicated growth was not quite fast enough to prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.
* Outdoor Systems agreed to buy Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing's billboard subsidiary for $1 billion.
* Dutch financial services firm ING Groep NV is in talks to purchase the 75 percent of investment bank Dillon Read it does not already own for as much as $450 million.
* General Motors and Chrysler announced their truck and car sales declined in April.
* The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is taking a cautious approach to regulating tobacco after last week's court ruling, which said the agency could regulate nicotine as a drug.
* America Online, CompuServe and Prodigy agreed to settle government allegations over their billing and marketing tactics.
* The main surprise surrounding an episode of a U.S. television series in which the main character reveals she is gay was the advertising lineup.
* Time Warner said it would unplug its interactive television network in Orlando, Florida by year-end.
* A foundation backed by financier George Soros has been fined by the Belarus government for what it alleged were currency violations.
* Market place: Fidelity Investments named James Curvey chief operating officer and chairman of the company's operating committee.
* News Corp executive Preston Padden, who led the company's bid to start a television-satellite service, resigned.
* Spain's government is disputing with the country's largest private media company over who will control Spain's pay-television industry.
